text:
alex: Heads up, ran into a case where runtime kept retrying the streaming fallback for a corrupted safetensors shard and we ended up thrashing the warmup cache. Need a clearer contract between loader verification and runtime warmup prioritization. Anyone seen this pattern?
mina: saw similar around 03:10 UTC yesterday. runtime attempted stream fallback 4x, then OOM while rehydrating the prefix cache. Manifest said chunk-size 4MB but blob was ~4.2MB.
jon: that sounds like either manifest-size drift or framing issue on the transport. Do we treat size mismatch as the same severity as checksum mismatch?
sara: logs looked like this: 
```
2026-03-20T03:10:12Z loader: shard read failed: expected 4194304 bytes, got 4404019
2026-03-20T03:10:12Z runtime: fallback -> stream-merge candidate selected
2026-03-20T03:10:12Z cache: eviction triggered during rehydrate, free=120MB
```
alex: proposal: introduce an advisory Warmup-Hint from runtime->loader and enforce a ManifestSanity (strict early checks) in loader that fails fast on checksum/size mismatch. If manifest sanity fails, runtime should select a different compatible bundle rather than repeatedly retrying the same shard.
mina: agreed on advisory hints, but please don't tie this to only HTTP headers. This should be in IPC/channel proto and sidecar wire too. Draft proto: 
```
WarmupHint {
  shard_id: string
  priority: int // 0 low, 1 normal, 2 hot
  verify_mode: "fast" | "full" // fast = length+crc32, full = blake3
  prefetch_window_ms: int
}
```
alex: semantics: verify_mode instructs loader which checks to run before returning a memory mapping. fast for immediate usage, full for background hydration. runtime can downgrade verify_mode adaptively if it sees sustained latency.
jon: tradeoffs: fast verify reduces tail latency but could let corrupted data through; full verify increases start latency and IO. We should emit telemetry to make policy decisions: metrics like shard_verify_mode, shard_verify_failures, shard_stream_retries, warmup_priority_latency.
sara: ops question: what should happen when verification fails? Do we mark the bundle bad and auto-roll back? Need a defined, low-noise playbook.
mina: suggested safety policy: on full-verify checksum fail -> mark bundle degraded, route new traffic to previous pinned version for 5 minutes, create alert. on fast-verify fail -> attempt streaming fallback once; if streaming also fails checksum -> mark degraded.
alex: add noise-suppression: only auto-degrade after failures on >=3 distinct hosts within 10m to avoid noisy pager for one-off network blips.
jon: exposing verify_mode in manifest might help bundle authors mark shards that are expensive to verify, but manifests are signed so we need a clear schema version bump and validation path for older runtimes.
sara: security note: manifests must continue to carry a cryptographic per-shard blake3 checksum. verify_mode is advisory for sync behavior only.
mina: perf note: full blake3 over a 200MB shard is ~150ms on our P4d NVMe, which is material for cold-start. mmap+on-demand page-in still has page fault cost. Full verify will affect start latency measurably.
alex: question: is returning zero-copy mmap safe if only fast verify passed? Risky. options: return a guarded mmap (invalid until full verify completes), or return copy-on-write buffer for fast starts.
jon: COW uses memory. Alternative: return mmap and mark kv-cache entries as "unverified" so runtime avoids using them for high-priority requests until verification completes. Adds complexity but saves memory.
sara: ops preference: start simple. Implement Warmup-Hint + fast verify returning a guarded mmap and runtime tags requests as lower-priority while unverified. Iterate on COW if memory pressure becomes an issue.
mina: please also add a small verification fence in the loader: if another local verifier is currently verifying the same shard, wait up to 200ms for it rather than spinning up duplicate downloads. That reduces thundering-herd.
alex: i'll draft an RFC covering Warmup-Hint wire schema, manifest flag, degraded-bundle policy, and required metrics. anyone want to co-author the perf section?
jon: i'll take perf benchmarks (blake3 vs crc32, mmap vs COW overhead).
sara: i'll write the rollback runbook appendix (who to notify, how to pin a previous bundle, quick scripts).
infra-bot: deploy-checklist: add an integration test to loader suite that simulates a corrupted chunk, verifies degraded marking, and checks runtime routes to fallback bundle.
mina: one more: for Private/On-prem installs, customers may elect to disable full verify for throughput. Need a config knob cascaded in Console with a clear warning.
alex: noted, RFC will include config knob and warning text. I'll publish draft by EOD and ping you for review. :thumbsup:
